config.Save deliberately does not validate, so this is the only check between a hand-edited config and the disk; a gate that never fires lets init rewrite a document that loads but means something the operator did not choose

the first byte of the derived key becomes a one-bit oracle on every failed login. The constant-time call is deliberately LEFT IN: a guard that only asks whether a ConstantTimeCompare exists is satisfied here, which is exactly how this shape got through once. TestKeyComparisonIsConstantTime is what kills it, by following the call's operands rather than their spelling.

the operands aliased out before the comparison, so the guard's watched set -- built from the call's operands -- never sees the names the oracle reads. The && short-circuits the constant-time call, making the first byte a one-bit oracle: the same defect as C1, one assignment away. Killed by propagateCopies, which extends the watched set with locals assigned from watched values. This is the reviewer's injection verbatim.

SURVIVES BY DESIGN, and is kept so the battery says so out loud. The oracle moved into a helper one function over: TestKeyComparisonIsConstantTime walks verifyWith's body, so a per-byte loop living in another function is never visited, while the constant-time call stays in place and the guard reads clean. Marked equivalent because no test in this set can distinguish it -- that is a statement about the guard's scope, not a claim the mutation is harmless. C3 is a real per-byte oracle and would be a real bug. Closing it needs the callee resolved and its body walked, which means go/types; the alternative is to accept that the guard covers one function body and say so in the test's doc comment, which is what was done. If go/types is ever added here, this entry must lose its equivalent flag and be made to die.

the config directory's ceiling is 0755 on purpose: a packager creates /etc/plock at the mode every other /etc subdirectory has, and the secret is the 0600 file inside. A tightened ceiling makes plock init refuse correctly configured machines

the shared floor stops being a floor: a 4-character admin password is accepted by both surfaces that can set one. It survived its first run for a reason worth keeping: this set's package is ./internal/auth/, and internal/auth only *defines* MinPasswordLen -- it enforces nothing, so no test in the suite the set runs can see the change. The mutant is therefore pinned at the enforcing suite with an explicit package override, and CI21 pins the same constant's other consumer. TestAShortNewPasswordIsRefusedByTheSameFloorAsTheCLI.
